item.title: Deriving Interplanetary Sector Boundary Crossings using Potential Field Source Surface Modeling
item.description: arXiv:2610.28123v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Heliospheric Current Sheet (HCS) and associated interplanetary sector boundaries fundamentally structure the solar wind environment, modulating coronal mass ejection (CME) evolution and solar energetic particle transport. In this study, we evaluate the capability of a static Potential Field Source Surface (PFSS; $R_{ss}=2.5R_\odot$) coronal model to directly map interplanetary sector boundary crossings from the Sun to 1 au without dynamic heliospheric propagation models. We compare ballistically transported HCS crossings derived from GONG-ADAPT and SDO/HMI magnetic maps against sector boundary crossing observations from the SBCross catalog. PFSS modeling reproduces the large-scale interplanetary magnetic field topology well ($J\approx0.50$), achieving hit rates (POD) of 0.64 for GONG-ADAPT and 0.76 for HMI. Carrington synoptic maps outperform flux-transport modeled maps, suggesting that the short-term observational noise from data assimilation degrades topological matching more than map "aging". Predictive skill shows a strong solar cycle dependence, performing significantly better during solar maxima (POD=0.70-0.81) than solar minima (POD=0.56-0.67), attributed to more distinct crossings due to higher HCS inclination angles during maximum. Matched events exhibit travel times close to ballistic estimates of 4.8-4.9 days with an average timing difference centered near zero ($\pm1.1$ days) and 90% of events within $\pm 1.8$ days. The hit rate of HCS structures that interact with CMEs does not degrade (POD = 0.67-0.83), despite propagating $\approx7$ hours faster on average, implying that the CME interaction causes only minor structural changes to the HCS. Larger timing differences (>24 hours) are associated with flatter current sheets. Overall, static PFSS extrapolations offer a computationally inexpensive, effective approach for mapping global sector boundary structure.
item.dc:creator: Stephan G. Heinemann, Manuela Temmer, Jens Pomoell, Mathew Owens, Emilia Kilpua, Matti ala-Lahti, Andreas Wagner

item.title: Detection and Statistics of large-scale Sector Boundary Crossings in the Solar Wind: The SBCross Catalog
item.description: arXiv:2610.28139v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Heliospheric sector boundary crossings (SBCs), composed of the Heliospheric Current Sheet (HCS), Heliospheric Plasma Sheet (HPS), and surrounding plasma halo, represent fundamental structures in the solar wind that influence interplanetary dynamics and space weather. We present the \textsc{SBCross} catalog, an automated, publicly available database containing 1,076 SBC events derived from in-situ observations spanning more than 30 years (1995--2026), covering Solar Cycles 23 and 24 alongside the rising and maximum phases of Solar Cycle 25. By combining interplanetary magnetic field (IMF) and 255~eV suprathermal electron pitch angle distributions (PAD) data, our algorithm reliably captures large-scale polarity transitions, with $76\%$ of detected SBCs exhibiting clear HPS signatures ($\beta > 1$, $n_{\mathrm{peak}} > 10\mathrm{\,cm^{-3}}$). Across the catalog, we find an average occurrence rate of $\approx 2.6$ events per Carrington rotation, a median event duration of $\approx 9.0$\,hours, and a median physical thickness of $\approx 7.4 \times 10^6$\,km. Furthermore, approximately $\approx 15\%$ of detected SBCs interact with interplanetary coronal mass ejections (CMEs) on average, with this proportion rising up to $33\%$ during solar maximum. These CME-associated events exhibit systematically longer durations (median of $10.0$\,hours), $54\%$ larger physical thicknesses, and higher average solar wind velocities. Notably, all high-velocity SBC events ($> 600\mathrm{\,km\,s^{-1}}$) are exclusively driven by CME interactions, demonstrating local plasma pile-up and structural entanglement resulting from fast CMEs overtaking the ambient slow background. The \textsc{SBCross} catalog serves as an updated successor to the classic SBC list by L. Svalgaard, delivering a standardized, open-access resource for the heliophysics community to systematically investigate sector boundary transitions.
item.dc:creator: Stephan G. Heinemann, Manuela Temmer, Mathew Owens, Emilia Kilpua, Charles Farrugia, Daniel Price

item.title: Real-Time 24-hour Ahead Forecasting of Solar Energetic Particle Events with SEPNET-PRISM-R
item.description: arXiv:2610.28292v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Solar energetic particle (SEP) events, operationally defined as proton flux exceeding 10 pfu in the >10 MeV channel, threaten spacecraft systems, astronaut safety, and high latitude aviation, yet continuous real-time forecasting with adequate lead time remains difficult. We present SEPNET-PRISM-R, a near-real-time system that issues hourly, 24 hour ahead probabilistic SEP forecasts. The model integrates multimodal solar data - including active region patches, flare features, coronal mass ejection (CME) characteristics, and historical proton flux - to concurrently predict SEP occurrences, peak proton flux, soft X-ray flux, and CME velocity, with the primary objective being SEP forecasting. Building on existing literature, SEPNET-PRISM-R enhances operational performance by incorporating a postprocessing module that enables cross-validated decision making and interpretable quantification of feature importance. The training dataset spans from February 1986 to September 2025, with subsequent forecasts generated sequentially through the present via a real-time space weather prediction platform that provides predictive probabilities, feature attributions, and historical analogs, enabling more reliable and informed operational decision-making. The proposed framework substantially suppresses false alarm rates while maintaining robust event detection capabilities, as evidenced by case studies and aggregate statistics.
item.dc:creator: Yian Yu, Yang Chen, Lulu Zhao, Kathryn Whitman, Ward Manchester, Tamas Gombosi

item.title: Exponential Growth of Turbulent Cross Helicity in Shear-Flow-Driven Turbulence
item.description: arXiv:2610.28424v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cross helicity, the velocity--magnetic-field correlation, is an ideal invariant of incompressible magnetohydrodynamics and constrains energy cascades and magnetic-field generation. Although cross helicity typically decays via visco-resistive effects, we analytically demonstrate that it grows exponentially in sheared inhomogeneous turbulence. This cross-helical shear instability is confirmed using three-dimensional numerical simulations. Growth requires a nonzero gradient of the Reynolds--Maxwell stress to produce turbulent cross helicity; this production overcomes effective losses when shear exceeds a threshold set by the ratio of turbulent magnetic to momentum diffusivities.
item.dc:creator: B. Tripathi, A. E. Fraser, P. W. Terry, E. G. Zweibel, M. J. Pueschel, A. M. Beloborodov

item.title: Automated optimization of solar energetic particle acceleration and transport parameters against five-spacecraft observations of the 9 October 2021 event
item.description: arXiv:2610.28603v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Solar energetic particle (SEP) events threaten space infrastructure, yet physics-based prediction models depend on numerous poorly constrained free parameters. We introduce the Fujitsu Solar Energetic particle Intelligent Tuning and Evaluation Network (SEITEN), which couples the SUSANOO MHD model of CME propagation to SEPIF, a diffusive shock acceleration and focused transport model, through the shock conditions SUSANOO supplies, and automatically optimizes the free parameters of the particle model against the SEP event of 9 October 2021. The mean free path and the injection efficiency vary independently along each magnetic field line and heliolongitudinal bin, giving a 19-dimensional problem solved by quasi-Monte Carlo sampling followed by a Tree-structured Parzen Estimator. The optimized model reproduces proton flux profiles at five spacecraft with a mean absolute error of $\approx 0.45$ in $\log_{10}$ flux, and the inferred mean free paths show a clear east-west structure; these are effective parameters conditional on the assumed transport geometry. Six independent runs show that whether mean free paths or injection efficiencies dominate depends on the MHD shock strength, and that injection efficiencies differ by orders of magnitude between MHD configurations despite nearly identical fit quality. Joint MHD-SEP parameter estimation is therefore a necessary next step towards generalized, operational SEP forecasting.
item.dc:creator: Hiroyuki Tako Ishikawa, Naho Fujita, Yuta Kato, Miki Kurihara, Takashi Minoshima, Daikou Shiota, Kazumasa Iwai, Marco Pinto, Ant\'onio Pessanha Gomes, Go Murakami, Kanya Kusano, Chihiro Mitsuda

item.title: Multifidelity Monte Carlo for Efficient Estimation of Drag-Coefficient Statistics in Rarefied Satellite Aerodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2604.21943v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Very-low-Earth-orbit analyses require reliable uncertainty estimates for the aerodynamic drag coefficient, but repeated direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) evaluations are expensive. We investigate whether cheaper collisionless models can reduce the computational cost of estimating DSMC-based drag statistics across different geometries. We also test whether improvements in the mean carry over to a variance reconstructed from two separately estimated raw moments. In the multifidelity Monte Carlo (MFMC) estimator, PICLas DSMC provides the high-fidelity response, while PICLAS test-particle Monte Carlo (TPMC) and the free-molecular Sentman panel model provide low-fidelity control variates. The benchmark contains four canonical Cube cases and scaled GOCE-like and CHAMP-like surface models. Each paired evaluation uses the same physical-input sample in all three models, and the reference values use 450 physically distinct DSMC evaluations per case. At the same estimation cost, DSMC-TPMC-Sentman MFMC reduces the RMSE of the mean drag coefficient in every tested case and budget, with median gains of 1.50-3.03. Variance estimation is less consistent: the three-model estimator improves three cases, performs close to HF-only Monte Carlo in two cases, and fails for GOCE-like. In that case, Sentman is only weakly correlated with the DSMC variance-related responses. Removing Sentman eliminates the negative estimates and improves the variance RMSE, although the decision to remove it was made after inspecting the results. MFMC therefore improves mean estimation reliably at reduced computational cost, but each low-fidelity model must be assessed separately for variance estimation.
item.dc:creator: Jovan Boskovic, Marcel Pfeiffer, Andrea Beck

item.title: Exact 1D Nonlinear Solutions for Proton-Driven Plasma Wakefields
item.description: arXiv:2607.06458v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend the classical 1D nonlinear relativistic plasma wakefield paradigm to evaluate the pristine fluid profiles driven by intense relativistic proton trains under the comoving coordinate approximation. Using an intense two-bunch scheme, our adaptive integration model is validated down to machine precision against exact closed-form cold-fluid invariants, confirming that interface boundary corners represent physical step discontinuities in the second potential derivative. Scaling to an $N=100$ micro-bunch train, we resolve macroscopic phase-accumulation and subsequent nonlinear detuning by deriving a closed-form, parameter-free piecewise analytical envelope expression. This solution successfully maps the initial unattenuated quadratic coherent growth alongside the flat asymptotic horizontal saturation horizon governed by nonlinear energy conservation. Furthermore, the framework analytically evaluates the transient envelope overshoot, tracking its decay onto the saturation boundary via an exact phase-slip integration length scale. Providing immediate, ready macro-envelope bounds, this computationally inexpensive tool eliminates empirical adjustments and yields a robust mathematical baseline designed to guide and accelerate complex, multi-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations through rapid parameter space exploration before deploying heavy computational assets. It establishes an efficient foundation to optimize asymmetric, custom-shaped driver profiles required to break the fundamental symmetric transformer ratio limit of 2 to make current particle accelerators more efficient.
item.dc:creator: D. Tsiklauri

item.title: Mechanical quality factor estimation from a nonlinear optical cavity response
item.description: arXiv:2609.07393v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Intrinsic damping rate and quality factor ($Q$) are key parameters in optomechanical systems. However, in high-Q devices, their measurement is often challenging because probe-induced dynamical backaction (DBA) and the need to resolve and accurately track the mechanical resonance limit the performance of state-of-the-art techniques. Here, we introduce an all-optical ringdown method in the unresolved-sideband regime that exploits the nonlinear, time-averaged optical response induced by strong mechanical motion. We derive an analytical model of the time-averaged optical cavity response probed by a weak frequency-scanning laser. During the evolution of the mechanical oscillator, the excited motion modulates the Lorentzian lineshape into a double-horned profile whose peak separation enables an accurate estimation of the modulation amplitude. Tracking this response during the mechanical ringdown allows the intrinsic damping rate to be determined without resolving the mechanical oscillation. We apply the method to a density-modulated phononic crystal membrane placed inside a high-finesse cavity and obtain mechanical quality factors consistent with independent measurements on the same platform. Our method requires a minimal optical setup, while offering an in situ diagnostic and reduced impact from probe-induced DBA and robustness against measurement noise. Finally, the model can describe other resonant systems dispersively coupled to coherent frequency modulations, providing new insights and measurement strategies that expand beyond the optomechanical platform.
item.dc:creator: Zohran Ali, Davide Tomasella, Daniel Allepuz-Requena, Alexander Huck, Ulrik Lund Andersen
